text:
ana: Heads-up, ran a 6h soak on rack-g3-12 after the node flapped. Started seeing repeated Xid 31s around 3.2h and a GPU ECC correction spike. Leaving notes here before I open a return ticket.

michael: Thx. Do we have the raw dmesg + nvml logs? Any thermal excursions or PDU events?

ana: attaching snippet from /var/log/soak/1987654321.log (copied):
```
[03:12:24] gpu0: Xid 31 at seq 4123, nvml: ECC correctable count increased by 72
[03:12:24] gpu0 temp: 72C (ambient rack 29C)
[03:12:25] gpustat: running 1 infer job, 15% util, mem 4.1GiB/24GiB
[03:12:26] ipmi: power-cycle issued by soak-harness (soft reset)
```

devon: Interesting — temp is high but not crazy. The ECC spike suggests transient memory errors rather than sustained thermal runaway. Did the soak-harness do a PCIe reset or a driver reload?

ana: soak-harness-bot: performed soft reset + nv driver reload at 3.3h, then Xids kept coming every ~2m for 10m, then quiet for 20m, then another cluster at 5.1h.

sam: Can we repro with targeted pattern? My worry: intermittent PCIe link flaps introduced by the riser or the slot. Suggest steps: 1) run repeat 30m memtest+stress on that slot 2) isolate to different riser (if available) 3) exercise thermal cycling in soakbench.

michael: Agreed. Also try toggling ECC scrubbing metrics collection to get per-page ECC corrected counts. If it's concentrated in addr ranges it points to DIMM/VRAM die. If spread, suspect PCIe.

ana: I'll run a focused memtest (memtest-gpu --pattern=walking-ones --repeat=500) on gpu0 with pci-stress enabled and capture nvml counters every 10s. Starting now, will post results in ~45m.

devon: FYI cross-region constraint: this rack is in us-west2 and spare riser inventory is low. If this is a riser swap we may need approval from hw-ops because it reduces available capacity for a day. Cost note: draining a node for riser-level RMA costs ~2k in carry/ops time (est).

sam: Good to surface the cost. If the memtest repros we'll tag for return; if it doesn't, try PCIe exerciser (pcie-flap-test) + kernel PCIe link retrain and re-run soak. Sometimes a firmware update on the BMC helped us before.

ana: memtest run finished. Output: 1) ECC corrected count increased in bursts (same pattern as earlier) 2) memtest reported 0 hard failures but increased corrected counts on pages around 0x7f3a2b0000-0x7f3a2b8fff.

michael: That page locality is telling. Likely VRAM die region on GPU0. Even without hard failures, repeated correctables are a sign we'll see hard errors under higher stress. Recommend quarantine and schedule return with vendor; create a replacement node and drain earlier to avoid app impact.

devon: Can we run a soak on same machine but move the GPU to different PCIe slot/riser (slot 3 -> slot 5) to check if the same addresses still spike? If the pattern moves with the card it's the card; if it stays, it's slot-level. Spare slot available next Tuesday.

ana: I'll attempt a hot-swap probe tomorrow in maintenance window: 1) cordon node, 2) stop workloads, 3) swap slot, 4) run 2h targeted memtest. If failure moves with the card -> return flow. If stays -> escalate to rack-level hw diagnostics.

soak-harness-bot: Note: automated ticket draft created: INF-2198 (attach logs + memtest output). Please add RMA tag if confirmed.

sam: One more datapoint — add thermal cycling with forced fan curve to stress VRAM temp gradients, that sometimes reveals microfractures. Keep ambient logs.

ana: Will do. I'll update INF-2198 after the slot probe. TL;DR: reproduces corrected ECC bursts focused on a VRAM address range; next step slot swap probe before RMA. :white_check_mark:
